Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:10:1.hebrew: אמר ליה רבא והא עדות מוכחשת היא - תימה: אמאי הואי עדות מוכחשת? והא רבא אית לי' במרובה (ב"ק ד' עב: ושם ד"ה רבא) ובפ' זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כז. ושם ד"ה רבא) דעד זומם מכאן ולהבא הוא נפסל, ולא מפסל אלא משעה דאתכחוש. ואית לן למימר: אאכילתה דאתכחוש אתכחוש, אאבהתא דלא אתכחוש לא אתכחוש. דהכי אמר במרובה (ב"ק דף עג. ושם): דהוזמו על הטביחה, ועל הגניבה לא הוזמו, אע"ג דתוך כדי דבור העידו על הגניבה ועל הטביחה; לרבא, כיון דמההיא שעתא דקא מיתזמי הוא דקא מיפסלי, אטביחה דאיתזום איתזום, על הגניבה דלא איתזום לא איתזום. וללישנא דהוי טעמא דרבא משום דעד זומם חידוש, ואין לך אלא משעת חידושו — ניחא. אלא ללישנא דמפרש טעמא דרבא משום פסידא דלקוחות, ה"נ נהימנינהו. ואפילו היכא דליכא פסידא דלקוחות לא מיפסל למפרע אפילו לההיא לישנא, מדבעי התם: מאי איכא בין האי לישנא להאי לישנא, ולא קאמר: איכא בינייהו להיכא דליכא פסידא דלקוחות. ועוד קשיא, דקאמר בסמוך אליבא דרב חסדא כולי עלמא לא פליגי, משמע דרב נחמן לא מצי סבר בשום ענין כרב חסדא דחשיב להו סהדי שקרי. ומנא ליה? דלמא סבר רב נחמן דמכאן ולהבא הוא נפסל! ומיהו הא איכא למימר משום דלא קיימא לן כרבא בהא. ונראה דסוגיא דהכא כההיא לישנא דחידוש; אבל ללישנא דפסידא דלקוחות, סבר דלא אמר ליה רבא לרב נחמן מעולם הכי. ולריב"א נראה דלא דמי הך דהכא לההיא דמרובה, דהתם גניבה וטביחה תרי מילי נינהו, ולהכי אגניבה דלא איתזום לא איתזום כיון דלהבא הוא נפסל; אלא הכא, כי איתכחוש אאכילה איתכחוש נמי אאבהתא, דאבהתא בלא אכילתה לא מהני, דהוי מוקמי' בידי' דאית ליה סהדי דאכלה שני חזקה, דנאמן לומר היתה של אבותי יום אחד במיגו דאי בעי אמר: מינך זבינתה. ומיהו אכתי דחשיב לה גמרא כעדות אחרת לא אתי שפיר:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:10:1.english: Rava said to him: "But this is contradicted testimony" - It is puzzling: Why is it contradicted testimony? Rava himself holds in Perek HaMarbeh (Bava Kamma 72b, s.v. Rava) and in the chapter Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 27a, s.v. Rava) that a conspiring witness (ed zomem) is disqualified only from now on, and is disqualified only from the moment he was contradicted. So we should say: regarding his eating [the produce of the field] they were contradicted; regarding the ancestors, about which they were not contradicted, they were not contradicted. For so it says in HaMarbeh (Bava Kamma 73a, there): [If witnesses] were found to be conspiring regarding the slaughter, but were not found to be conspiring regarding the theft, even though they testified about the theft and the slaughter within the span of a single utterance — according to Rava, since they are disqualified only from that moment on, regarding the slaughter, about which they were found conspiring, they are found conspiring, and regarding the theft, about which they were not found conspiring, they are not found conspiring. Now, according to the version [of the Gemara there] that Rava's reason is because [the law of] a conspiring witness is a novelty (chiddush), and you have only [the effect] from the time of its novelty — this works well. But according to the version that explains Rava's reason as being due to the loss that would befall purchasers, here too we should believe them. And even where there is no loss to purchasers, he is not disqualified retroactively, even according to that version, since the Gemara there asks, "What is the difference between this version and that version?" and does not say, "The difference between them is where there is no loss to purchasers." Furthermore, there is another difficulty: that [the Gemara] says shortly afterward, "According to Rav Chisda, everyone agrees," implies that Rav Nachman could not, under any circumstances, hold like Rav Chisda, who considers them false witnesses. But how does he know [this]? Perhaps Rav Nachman holds that [a conspiring witness] is disqualified only from now on! However, one could say [that Rav Nachman rejected Rava's argument] because we do not rule like Rava in this matter. And it appears that the sugya here follows that version [which holds that the law of conspiring witnesses is] a novelty; but according to the version of loss to purchasers, [Rav Nachman] holds that Rava never said this to Rav Nachman. And the Riva (Rabbi Yitzchak ben Asher) thinks that this case does not resemble that of HaMarbeh: there, theft and slaughter are two separate matters, and therefore regarding the theft, about which they were not found conspiring, they are not found conspiring, since they are disqualified only for the future. Here, however, when they were contradicted regarding the eating, they were contradicted also regarding the ancestors, for [a claim of] ancestors without eating is of no avail — for we would be establishing [the field] in the possession of one who has witnesses that he ate it for the years of chazakah, who is believed to say, "It belonged to my ancestors for one day," by virtue of a migo, since had he wished, he could have said, "I bought it from you." But still, [the fact] that the Gemara considers it like other testimony does not fit well.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:1:1.hebrew: אבל אכלה שית שנין כו' - הקשה ר"י בר מרדכי: אפי' לא אייתי סהדי אלא דאכלה שלש שנין, יהא נאמן לומר "לקחתיה קודם מינך", במיגו דאי בעי אמר "מינך זבינתה"? ואומר ר"י דאין זה מיגו, דמעיקרא לא יטעון כלל "מינך זבינתה", דאין יודע אם יש לזה שטר שקנאה ממנו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:1:1.english: But if he consumed [the produce] for six years, etc. - Rabbi Yitzchak ben Mordechai asked: Even if [the possessor] brought witnesses only that he consumed [the produce] for three years, he should be believed to say, "I bought it before [I bought it from] you," by virtue of a *migo* — for if he wished, he could have said, "I bought it from you"? But Rabbi Yitzchak says that this is not a *migo*, because at the outset he would not claim at all, "I bought it from you," since he does not know whether this [other party] has a deed showing that he acquired it from him.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:2:1.hebrew: אמר רבה מה לו לשקר - רבה גרסינן, דאביי ורבא אמרי לקמן (בבא בתרא דף לג:) דלא סבירא להו הא דרב חסדא, דמה לי לשקר במקום עדים לא אמרינן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:2:1.english: Rabbah said: Why would he lie? - We read "Rabbah," for Abaye and Rava say below (Bava Batra 33b) that they do not hold this [principle] of Rav Chisda, [and that the argument] "why would I lie" we do not apply where there are witnesses.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:3:1.hebrew: מה לי לשקר במקום עדים לא אמרינן - תימה לרשב"א: אמאי הוי במקום עדים? נימא: של אבותיו היתה יום אחד, ונאמר שלקחה מאבותיו, דהא טוענין ליורש! ומהימנינן ליה בהא דקאמר שאבותיו דרו בו יום אחד, במיגו דאי בעי אמר: מינך זבנתיה. ולקמן נמי, דקאמרי נהרדעי דהיכא דאמר "של אבותי שלקחוה מאבותיך" דחוזר וטוען — הא אפילו לא יטעון שלקחוה, אלא אמר שדרו בה יום אחד, אנן טענינן ליה! ואומר רבינו יצחק דשל אבותי משמע שהיתה מעולם של אבותי, ולא שלקחוה עד שיפרש בדבריו. ולקמן דנקט "שלקחוה" — לא שצריך שיטעון שידע שלקחוה, אלא "של אבותי", שראיתי שדרו בה יום אחד, על כן אני רוצה לזכות, דשמא לקחוה אבותי במשפט, וטוענין ליורש:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:3:1.english: "What reason do I have to lie?" — we do not say [this] where there are witnesses - Rashba found this astonishing: Why is this a case of [contradicting] witnesses? Let us say: It was his fathers' for one day, and let us say that [his fathers] bought it from [the claimant's] fathers, for we argue on behalf of an heir! And we believe him in this, when he says that his fathers lived in it for one day, by virtue of a migo: for if he wished, he could have said, "I bought it from you." And below as well, where the Nehardeans say that when he said, "It is of my fathers, who bought it from your fathers," he may retract and make a [new] claim — but even if he does not claim that they bought it, and says only that they lived in it for one day, we argue on his behalf! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that "of my fathers" implies that it was of my fathers from time immemorial, and not that they bought it, unless he specifies so in his words. And below, where [the Gemara] says "that they bought it," it is not that he must claim that he knows they bought it; rather [he says], "It is of my fathers," because I saw that they lived in it for one day, and therefore I wish to establish my right, for perhaps my fathers took it by [a court] ruling — and we argue on behalf of an heir.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:7:1.hebrew: ומודו נהרדעי היכא דאמר שלקחוה כו' - מספקא לר"י: היכא דנפיק לבראי וחזר ואתא לב"ד, אי מצי למימר הכי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:7:1.english: "And the Nehardeans agree where he said, 'that they bought it,' etc." - Ri was uncertain: where [the defendant] went outside and returned to the court, whether he is able to say this.
